title: Align migration-manifest CurrencyUnitSemantics with the dataset providers so the 13 drifted fixed/dynamic entries can reach parity-passed
description: Stage 2 parity defect: ReportMigrationRegistry.SemanticsMatch (src/ERP.Application/Services/ReportMigrationRegistry.cs:172-183) compares definition.CurrencyUnitSemantics (compile-time manifest in src/ERP.Application/DTOs/ReportMigrationRegistryDtos.cs) to dataset.CurrencyUnitSemantics (runtime dataset provider) using exact ordinal equality. Seven datasets' manifest declarations drifted from their providers' precise currency/unit semantics strings, so 13 manifest entries fail SemanticsMatch and are permanently stuck at preset-ready — never advancing to parity-passed even with complete four-dimension evidence. Affected: report/dynamic:product-sales-ranking, report/dynamic:order-profit, report/dynamic:salesman-output, report/dynamic:sales-commission, report/dynamic:follow-up-due, report/dynamic:quotation-conversion, dynamic:receivable. Fix the manifest literals to exactly match each provider's CurrencyUnitSemantics string (provider is the authoritative implemented semantics), preserving the fail-closed ordinal comparison and never weakening the four-dimension evidence gate (DataGrainMatched + CurrencyUnitMatched + PermissionsMatched + OutputSemanticsMatched). No new controller/designer/exporter, no arbitrary SQL, no schema/seed/migration, no secrets/env, no permission expansion; only the manifest DTO plus regression tests. Not audit-only: unblocks correct parity derivation for 13 genuinely migrated entries.
acceptance_criteria: The 13 drifted manifest entries (report:product-sales-ranking, dynamic:product-sales-ranking, report:order-profit, dynamic:order-profit, report:salesman-output, dynamic:salesman-output, report:sales-commission, dynamic:sales-commission, report:follow-up-due, dynamic:follow-up-due, report:quotation-conversion, dynamic:quotation-conversion, dynamic:receivable) carry CurrencyUnitSemantics exactly equal to their dataset providers' CurrencyUnitSemantics, so SemanticsMatch returns true for those entries when menu and currency/unit both match.

No entry reaches parity-passed without complete four-dimension evidence (DataGrainMatched + CurrencyUnitMatched + PermissionsMatched + OutputSemanticsMatched); the existing single-dataset and bundle parity derivation, multi-menu RequiredMenuCodesMatch, and CompatibilityDeclared checks are unchanged and remain fail-closed.

Add/update executable unit coverage asserting the manifest CurrencyUnitSemantics equals the dataset provider CurrencyUnitSemantics for the 13 drifted entries, that already-matching entries (customer-shipment, container-stats, inventory-movement, inventory-aging, ar-aging, purchase-cost, tax-refund-summary, balance-sheet, income-statement, cash-flow, stock-alert, agency-service-fee-monthly, receipt-reconciliation, purchase-order, supplier-aging, supplier-exposure, shipment-finance, sales-order, product-export-field-completeness, trade-document) remain unchanged, and that SemanticsMatch still fails closed on any currency/unit mismatch. Run the related tests plus the safe Release build/unit suite and scheduler self-test/contracts.
implementation_evidence: src/ERP.Application/Services/ReportMigrationRegistry.cs:178-181 SemanticsMatch uses string.Equals(definition.CurrencyUnitSemantics, dataset.CurrencyUnitSemantics, StringComparison.Ordinal).
